Data sources and freshness

How to read this forecast

The headline begins with each district’s 2024 presidential margin, applies the national swing implied by current generic-ballot polling, and adds the expected Alabama legislative difference from that federal baseline.

That down-ballot adjustment reflects generic legislative lag, incumbency, and the observed fundraising difference between the Democratic and Republican candidates. The Dem and Rep scenarios show how a typical national polling error would move the forecast.

Full methodologyHistorical WAR modelDistrict scenariosHistorical test
Forecast uncertainty.

The headline uses 50,000 correlated simulations. Shared national, statewide, and chamber error prevents the chamber distribution from treating every district as independent.

District probabilities use a Student-t(5) curve with a 5.75-point scale. Scenario tabs show a typical national polling error in either direction.

The full candidate adjustment has one direct forward test, from 2018 to 2022. Districts with one major-party nominee are fixed; genuinely unresolved districts remain unmodeled and gray.
